source.name: Chuck's Guide to the A-10C Warthog
source.version_or_date: Last Updated: 31/08/2023 (as printed in the PDF header, page 1) - re-check chucksguides.com periodically for a newer edition

_extraction_note: Checklist steps are Part 4 (Start-Up Procedure) copied directly from the guide's own numbered steps, not generated. The guide covers both the A-10C Legacy and A-10C II Tank Killer in one document, calling out the few steps where they differ (only step 10, radio setup) - the Tank Killer Expansion variant text was used throughout since that's the module this file is for; the Legacy-only radio steps were left out as not applicable. Two ground-crew interphone calls that precede numbered step 1 in the guide (retract ladder, remove chocks) are included as unnumbered steps '0a'/'0b'. IMPORTANT: this guide has no standalone engine-shutdown/post-flight checklist anywhere (verified against the full 18-part table of contents and a full-text search of the extracted PDF) - Part 6 'Landing' ends at touchdown and Part 7 moves straight into engine systems/fuel management, same gap already noted in the AH-64D file. The 'shutdown' list below is intentionally empty rather than guessed. Weapons are Part 10 (Offence: Weapons & Armament), copied/closely paraphrased from the guide's own lettered/numbered attack sequences (A/B/C.../1/2/3...), not generated. Where a weapon has two release-mode variants that share an identical DSMS profile-setup procedure (e.g. MK-82's manual-CCIP vs. CCIP-CR release), the shared setup is written once and the two attack procedures are both included rather than duplicating the setup steps twice - no steps were invented or altered, just de-duplicated. AGM-65L Laser Maverick, GBU-54 Laser JDAM, and APKWS are marked 'Tank Killer Only' in the guide itself and match this file's module. Ordnance jettison (Part 10 section 4) is included as its own list. 'taxi' (Part 5, Taxi section) and 'takeoff' (Part 5, Takeoff section) checklists, and the 'landing' checklist (Part 6, Normal 360-Degree Landing Approach), are copied directly from the guide's own short numbered steps, same as Part 4 - each restarts its own 1-N numbering rather than continuing Part 4's global count, matching how the guide itself numbers them. The AoA Indexer systems_notes entry is NOT from the guide - it's written independently (standard real-world AoA-indexer symbology, described in different terms/words than the guide's own ASCII arrow representation) since it's directly relevant to flying the landing approach above. Deliberately NOT converting the rest of the guide's ~18 parts wholesale (Parts 1-3, 7-8, 11-18 - cockpit/controls reference, engine/fuel, RWR/countermeasures, datalink, radio, autopilot/LASTE, navigation, air-to-air refueling) - that would mean reproducing the bulk of a commercial, copyrighted guide rather than a few short procedural excerpts. 'night_vision_goggles' (Part 3's short NVG keybind reference) and 'night_flying_ground_prep' (explicit request: the 5-item 'things to do on the ground' list from Part 5's own PRE-FLIGHT section, page 123) are both condensed/paraphrased from their respective short reference sections - not verbatim guide prose - and each of the 5 ground-prep items pulls its actual how-to steps from that item's own short dedicated subsection elsewhere in the guide (TAD Own ID setup p.124, DSMS reload p.126, CMS countermeasure programs p.400, ARC-210/UHF radio tuning p.431/435-436) rather than being invented. Part 9 (Sensors) is explicit request ('pull in the sensors section') and is fully covered by the 11 new checklists 'hud_target_designation' through 'hmcs_markpoint_creation' (each guide subsection - 1.3 HUD/TDC, 2.4-2.8 TGP start-up/lasing/steerpoint-slave/boresight/laser-spot-search/laser-pointer, 4.2/4.5 HMCS power-up/profiles/hook/SPI/TGP-slave/markpoint - condensed/paraphrased from its own short numbered procedure, not verbatim) plus 5 new systems_notes entries (SOI/SPI concept, TGP HOTAS reference, Maverick sensor overview, HMCS symbology categories, HMCS HOTAS reference) that are ALL written independently in different words/structure than the guide's own diagram-legend and prose explanations, not paraphrased from them. 1.4 TISL/Pave Penny (Legacy-only, and explicitly 'not functionally implemented in this simulation' per the guide itself) was excluded as not applicable, same as other Legacy-only content elsewhere in this file. New binding_key identifiers introduced for this addition: china_hat_aft, coolie_hat_down. Part 11 (Defence: RWR and Countermeasures) is explicit request ('countermeasures') - the chaff/flare CMS programs (A/B/C/D, MANUAL/AUTO) were already covered in night_flying_ground_prep, so this pass adds the 3 remaining pieces as systems_notes, all written independently rather than paraphrased: ECM jammer modes (AIR/SAM1/SAM2/AAA), how to read the RWR display (circle proximity/state meanings), and MWS states. The guide's own 'RWR Symbol List' (page 403, credited to a third party '.408-X~RAY') is a table/image the PDF extraction did not capture any readable text for - skipped rather than guessed at from general knowledge, since inventing specific symbol-to-threat-type mappings would risk being wrong. The guide's 'Art of Defeating a Missile' section is just a list of external links (YouTube videos, other websites) with no A-10-specific content of its own - skipped as not applicable to this file's data. Part 12 (Datalink/SADL) is explicit request ('data link') and is fully covered by 8 new checklists - 'sadl_network_setup' (Group/Own ID/callsign) plus the guide's own 7 lettered SADL Functions A-G ('sadl_hook_symbol' through 'sadl_receive_jtac_tasking'), each condensed/paraphrased from its own short numbered procedure, not verbatim - plus 2 new systems_notes (SADL overview, SADL symbology) written independently. 'sadl_broadcast_spi' step 5 (broadcast to the whole network) uses only the Tank Killer control (TMS LEFT LONG) - the guide's Legacy-variant control (DMS LEFT LONG) was left out, same exclusion pattern as elsewhere in this file. New binding_key identifier introduced: tms_left. Part 13 (Radio) is explicit request ('radio') and is covered by 5 new checklists, each condensed/paraphrased from its own short numbered tutorial in the guide: radio_arc210_manual_frequency and radio_arc210_preset_channel (ARC-210 Tutorials 1-2), radio_arc210_edit_preset (Tutorial 3, programming a preset channel with a briefed frequency), radio_arc186_vhf_fm (the JTAC radio), and radio_arc164_uhf (the flight/wingman radio, plus its own load-a-preset sub-procedure). The Legacy-only AN/ARC-186(V) VHF AM #1 tutorial was excluded - per the guide's own Tank Killer radio overview, that radio 'is not installed on the A-10C II Tank Killer variant' (ARC-210 replaces it), same exclusion pattern as elsewhere in this file. Also skipped: the 'Advanced radio tutorial' line, just a link to an external PDF with no content of its own, and the Caucasus-map airfield tower frequency table (explicit call: real, useful data, but specific to one theater/map - would be actively misleading presented as universal advice in a per-aircraft file with no theater awareness, so left out entirely rather than included with a caveat). 3 new systems_notes entries (radio system overview, Intercom Panel, which ARC-210 controls do nothing in DCS) are written independently, not paraphrased. New binding_key identifiers introduced: mic_switch_forward, mic_switch_aft, mic_switch_down. Part 17 (Air-to-Air Refueling) is explicit request ('A2A') and is covered by one 17-step checklist ('air_to_air_refueling'), condensed/paraphrased from the guide's own numbered 'How To' procedure, plus one new systems_notes entry (tanker compatibility - the A-10C's boom-only refueling door means only the KC-135 works in DCS, not the probe-and-drogue tankers). Real, confirmed gap in the source material, handled per explicit instruction rather than guessed at: step 4 of the guide's procedure (contact the tanker) specifies the Legacy A-10C's VHF AM #1 radio, which this file's own Radio system overview note already establishes is NOT installed on the Tank Killer variant - the guide never states what replaces it for tanker comms on Tank Killer, and this has not been verified in-game, so that step is written as an honest, explicit open gap rather than a guessed answer. Skipped the guide's own 'Why We All Hate It' intro (personal opinion/narrative, not reference data) and its two external links (a YouTube example, a Steam Community written tutorial) - neither is A-10-specific content to source from. Part 16 (Navigation & ILS Landing) is explicit request ('nav') and is the largest single addition so far - 16 new checklists condensed/paraphrased from the guide's own numbered procedures (waypoint designate/navigate/consult/add/edit/offset, markpoint navigate/consult/add, flight plan create/use, divert, ADF, TACAN, anchor point setup, ILS approach) plus 7 new systems_notes written independently (nav systems overview, NMSP, TAD moving map, TAD HOTAS reference, HSI reference, navigation point types, bullseye call format). The guide's own worked examples throughout this part use specific mission/map data (Groom Lake AFB coordinates, Kutaisi's TACAN channel, Khasab/Batumi airfields, specific frequencies like 255.000 MHz) purely to illustrate a real walkthrough - none of that was carried in as fact; every checklist here is written generically (e.g. 'the beacon's frequency, from your mission briefing' instead of a hardcoded number), same principle as the Caucasus airfield frequency table excluded from the Radio addition. ils_landing_approach deliberately stops at 'deploy gear/flaps/airbrakes' and points back at the existing 'landing' checklist for the touchdown sequence rather than re-describing it - the guide's own ILS section duplicates that content almost verbatim (itself an artifact of the guide's page numbering restarting mid-section). Excluded the Legacy-only TAD control mapping (6.1's 'CONTROLS (A-10C LEGACY)') in favor of the Tank Killer one, same pattern as elsewhere. New binding_key identifier introduced: dms_up_down (DMS UP/DOWN - cycling waypoints/markpoints/airfields - a third DMS axis distinct from the existing dms_fwd_aft and dms_left_right). Remaining flight_planning_notes and qa_snippets are still empty/not curated. Weapons audit (explicit request: 'missing weapons instructions', CBU-87 named as the example). Root cause of the gap: pages 235-238 of the guide - Rob10's seven 'Weapons Usage' quick-reference charts (Guns, Rockets, Unguided Bombs x2, Guided Bombs, Maverick, Air-to-Air) - are image-only, so they came out blank in the text extraction (draft_dcs_a10c2.txt) and were never read; they were rendered and read directly from the PDF instead. The charts explicitly name weapons that have no numbered 2.x section of their own: MK-84, CBU-87 and CBU-97 (Unguided Ordnance Usage) and GBU-10, GBU-31 and CBU-103 (Guided Ordnance Usage). Added six weapon entries for those (all condensed/paraphrased from the chart procedures; CBU-87/CBU-97/CBU-103 parameters from section 2.7), CCRP rocket delivery steps on the Hydra entry, gun range guidance on the GAU-8 (air-to-ground) entry, Targeting-Pod A-A and extra seeker-control steps on the AIM-9 entry, and Part 10's general chapters that had not been carried over: 6 systems_notes (DSMS overview, DSMS station color coding, HUD master modes, CCIP vs CCRP, consent-to-release modes, the basic fire-a-weapon sequence) and the 'dsms_reload_after_rearm' checklist (guide section 1.4). Known limits, stated rather than papered over: (1) the guide's click-by-click on the INV STAT page shows HoF only - the RPM setting for the CBU-87/CBU-103 is described but never walked through, so those steps assume it sits beside HOF (flagged in the CBU-87 employment_notes; verify in-game); (2) the GBU-10 and GBU-31 have no walkthrough of their own - their setup is written as 'same as the GBU-12 / GBU-38' plus the chart's release steps, said so in each entry's employment_notes; (3) the charts are an older revision (Rev 1.0.6) than the numbered procedures, flagged on the AIM-9 additions where a control differs. Skipped: the chart's Maverick page (already covered by the section 2.9/2.10 entries, including the flaps-up warning) and the guide's HOTAS control tables for section 1.2 (OCR-garbled beyond reliable use; the per-weapon steps already carry the button names).

pre_start.action: Request the ground crew to retract the boarding ladder over the interphone: press \ (Communication Menu), select Ground Crew (F8), select 'Stow boarding ladder' (F4).
Request the ground crew to remove the wheel chocks over the interphone: press \ (Communication Menu), select Ground Crew (F8), select 'Wheel Chocks' (F5), select 'Remove' (F2).
Emergency Flood Lights - ON (if doing a night operation).
Hold the Signal Lights Lamp Test switch and confirm the caution light panel is functioning.
Hold the OXY IND TEST switch and confirm the LOW OXY warning message is displayed and audible.
Hold the Test Fuel Indicator switch to confirm the fuel indicator is working properly.
Close the canopy by holding the canopy switch DOWN (right click, or LCTRL+C).

Set up radios (A-10C II Tank Killer Expansion): a) Set ARC-210 V/UHF Radio to TR (Transmit-Receive). b) Set UHF radio to MAIN. c) Set VHF FM Radio #2 to TR (Transmit-Receive). d) Set proper radio frequencies as required.
Boost pumps for MAIN and WING tanks - ON.

apu_start.action: Wait until APU RPM reaches 100%, then set the APU Generator switch - ON. Note: the APU generator supplies electrical power to the engine, and APU bleed air drives the engine starter.

engine_start.action: Verify both Engine Operation switches are in the NORM position.

Crank up the left engine by moving the left throttle from OFF to IDLE (RALT+HOME). This automatically initiates a left engine start with automatic ignition; once the throttle is at IDLE, the DC fuel boost pumps activate to feed that engine. Note: on the Warthog Throttle HOTAS you need to physically raise/pull up the throttle.
During start, the ENG START CYCLE indication will be visible.
Confirm oil pressure increases during start. ITT (Interstage Turbine Temperature) will spike at 900°C but should stabilize between 275 and 865°C.
Wait until the engine spools up to a stabilized core RPM of 56% when idling on the ground. Monitor left hydraulic system pressure build-up, which should normalize between 2,800 and 3,350 PSI.
When the engine reaches IDLE RPM, hydraulic pumps kick in and oil pressure stabilizes; the L-GEN, L-HYD PRESS and L-ENG OIL PRESS cautions will extinguish.
When the Master Caution warning sound is heard, click the MASTER CAUTION switch.
Crank up the right engine by moving the right throttle from OFF to IDLE (RCTRL+HOME). Wait until it spools up to IDLE settings as above.

post_start.action: Set the Pitot Heat Switch - ON (FWD).
Set the CDU (Control Display Unit) switch - ON.
Set the EGI (Embedded GPS-INS) switch - ON.
Once the EGI switch is ON, navigation system alignment starts and takes approx. 4 minutes. Status can be monitored on the CDU ALIGN sub-page (MFCDs are not powered yet).
Uncage the Standby Attitude Indicator (SAI).
Turn ON the left and right MFCD (Multi-Function Color Display) screens by left-clicking twice on each power switch.
Set the CICU (Central Interface Control Unit) switch - ON. The MFCDs will turn blue.
Set the JTRS (Joint Tactical Radio System) switch - ON. JTRS powers Situational Awareness Datalink (SADL), which helps identify friendly/enemy forces on your displays.
Set the IFFCC (Integrated Flight & Fire Control Computer) switch - TEST (middle position).
Press ENT on the UFC (Up Front Controller) to engage Preflight BIT. This runs an automated Built-In Test taking about 1 minute.
Once BIT is complete, press ENT on the UFC to exit the PREFLIGHT BIT menu.
Scroll down the HUD menus using SEL and select EXIT by pressing ENT on the UFC.
Set the IFFCC switch - ON (UP position).
Pitch and Yaw SAS (Stability Augmentation System) switches - ON.
Hold the TAKEOFF TRIM switch for 1-2 seconds. This sets all trim tabs to neutral takeoff settings; the TAKEOFF TRIM light above the button illuminates once set.

Once a DTS UPLOAD page appears on the MFCD (Data Transfer System), press the OSB (Option Selection Button) next to 'Load All' to load the DTS cartridge - mission waypoints, weapon data, bullseye data and other nav data set up in the mission editor. Takes about 15 seconds.
Once the DTS cartridge is loaded, the white DSMS, INVT and CMBT cautions disappear and an asterisk appears next to every menu (* means loaded).
Select the OSB next to CDU on the right MFCD to display EGI Alignment data on that screen. Once the alignment status timer reads 'T = 4.0 0.8', the EGI is aligned.
Set the STEERPOINT selector to FLIGHT PLAN. This enables using waypoints on the HUD and TAD to navigate.
On the right MFCD (with CDU data displayed), select NAV mode by pressing the OSB next to the NAV menu. An asterisk appears once NAV mode is selected.
Select the OSB next to TAD (Tactical Awareness Display) on the left MFCD to display TAD data on that screen.
Set CMS (Countermeasures) mode to MAN.
Set the MWS (Missile Warning System), JMR (ECM Jammer), RWR (Radar Warning Receiver) and DISP (Countermeasure Dispenser) switches - ON.
Engage Nosewheel Steering (pinky switch on the HOTAS stick, or the INSERT key).
Set the Anti-Skid Switch - ON.
Select EGI navigation mode.
Set the EAC (Enhanced Attitude Control) Switch - ARMED.
Set the RDR ALTM (Radar Altimeter) Switch - NORMAL.
Arm the ejection seat (lever DOWN). The SEAT NOT ARMED caution should disappear.
Check the caution panel - any message still displayed will tell you if you forgot something.
(A-10C II Tank Killer only) Set the Scorpion HMCS (Helmet-Mounted Cueing System) Power Switch - ON (FWD).

taxi.action: Confirm Nosewheel Steering is engaged (pinky switch on the HOTAS stick, or the INSERT key).
Move the throttles forward slowly as required to start moving.
Steer left/right with the rudder pedals - do not use differential braking to steer.
Keep taxi speed between 15 and 25 knots.
Do not open or close the canopy while turning.
Use the toe brakes to slow and stop the aircraft.

takeoff.action: In cold conditions, confirm Pitot Heat is ON.
Press the TAKEOFF TRIM switch to confirm you're trimmed for takeoff.
Set flaps for takeoff (MVR, middle position, 7 deg) and confirm speedbrakes are retracted.
Hold the brakes and advance to MAX throttle.
Release the brakes and start the takeoff roll.
Disengage Nosewheel Steering (OFF) once you reach 70 kts.
Rotate at 135 kts: set the Landing Gear Lever UP and set Flaps UP.
Climb out at 10 units AoA (Angle of Attack) - don't yank back on the stick; let the aircraft fly off the runway on its own.

landing.action: Before glide path (final approach): extend airbrakes to 40%, lower the landing gear, set flaps DOWN (fully extended).
On glide path (final approach): maintain a descent rate of about -500 ft/min.
Touchdown: let the aircraft settle onto the runway - no flare needed.

dsms_reload_after_rearm.action: Select any page on the right MFCD.
Press and hold the MSG OSB until the DISPLAY PROGRAM page appears.
Press the LOAD OSB on the right-hand menu.
Press the lower MSG OSB - it replaces the MSG page with the LOAD page.
Press the new lower LOAD OSB to select the DTS (Data Transfer System) UPLOAD page.
Press LOAD ALL on the right to reload every DSMS station.
While the DTC is loading, the asterisks beside the menus being reloaded disappear - wait for it to finish.

When loading completes, asterisks appear next to every menu again and the DSMS pages show the correct ordnance. (Do this after every re-arm: the ground crew installs a fresh Data Transfer Cartridge (DTC) with the new ordnance, but the DSMS has to reload it before its station data is updated.)

night_vision_goggles.action: Toggle Night Vision Goggles ON/OFF: RSHIFT + H.
Increase NVG brightness: RCTRL + RSHIFT + H.
Decrease NVG brightness: RALT + RSHIFT + H.

night_flying_ground_prep.action: Identify yourself on the TAD and give your wingmen a way to see you: a) Select the NET OSB on the TAD. b) Enter your desired ID number on the UFC scratchpad. c) Press the OWN ID OSB to apply it. d) Return to the TAD view via the TAD OSB. Anyone sharing your Group ID then sees your Own ID appear on their own TAD - useful for coordinating position in the dark without needing visual contact.

Program your weapons on the DSMS. If you changed your loadout after spawning, reload it first: select the CDU OSB on the right MFCD, press and hold the MSG OSB until the DISPLAY PROGRAM menu appears, select LOAD, then LOAD ALL - reload is complete once an asterisk appears next to every menu. Then set up each weapon's release profile (mode, fuzing, ripple, offsets, laser code, etc.) - see this file's own Weapons list for the specific DSMS steps per munition.

Set up your countermeasure programs on the CMSP, or just pick a preset: Program A (older-generation radar SAM), Program B (newer-generation radar SAM), Program C (IR heat-seeking SAM), Program D (general-purpose/unknown threat). Cycle programs with the CMS switch RIGHT/LEFT, and choose MANUAL (you decide when to run it) or AUTO (the system picks and runs the best program for whatever's detected) on the CMS Mode Selector.

Set your radio frequencies from the mission briefing before you need them. On the ARC-210: set Radio Operation Mode - TR, Frequency Mode - MAN (manual) or PRST (preset), SQL - ON, then dial in the frequency (or select the preset channel) - it's confirmed once it shows on the V1 HUD readout. To save a briefed frequency onto a preset channel on the older UHF radio: dial in the frequency, select the destination preset channel, and press LOAD.

Review your flight plan before takeoff: check your waypoints/steerpoints on the TAD (and the CDU's flight-plan page) so you already know the route instead of working it out for the first time in the dark.

hud_target_designation.action: Set the Master Mode Switch to NAV mode.
Press Coolie Hat UP to set the HUD as the Sensor of Interest (SOI).
By default the TDC (Target Designation Cue) is caged on the Total Velocity Vector (TVV).
Use the Slew Control Switch to move the TDC onto the target.
Press TMS FWD LONG to set the TDC's current location as the SPI (Sensor Point of Interest).
To reset the SPI, press TMS AFT LONG - the TDC stays ground-stabilized where it was.
To recage the TDC back to the TVV, press China Hat AFT SHORT.

tgp_startup_and_lasing.action: Press the OSB next to TGP to bring up the TGP feed page.
On the AHCP, set the TGP switch ON (UP) to power up the targeting pod.
Wait through the roughly 2-minute warm-up - the display shows TGP OFF, then NOT TIMED OUT during warm-up.
Warm-up is complete once the NOT TIMED OUT indication disappears.
Set MASTER ARM and LASER ARM switches to ARM.
Select A-G (Air-to-Ground) TGP mode by pressing the OSB next to AG.
Confirm the TGP switches from STBY to AG mode - the camera un-stows.
Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TGP feed to set the TGP as SOI.
Select the video mode with the Boat Switch: FWD = FLIR Black Hot, MIDDLE = CCD (TV), AFT = FLIR White Hot.
Select Field-of-View with China Hat FWD SHORT (toggles WIDE/NARROW).
Select the desired Laser Designator Mode (LSR) with its OSB.
Press the OSB next to CNTL to enter the TGP A-G Control Page.
Enter the desired laser code on the UFC scratchpad (e.g. 1688).
Press the OSB next to "L" (Laser Designation Code) to apply the code.
Select the desired LATCH mode with its OSB (ON = laser stays firing once triggered by the Nosewheel Steering Button; OFF = you must hold the button).
Press the OSB next to RTN to return to the main TGP page.
Use the Slew Control Switch to move the TGP reticle onto the target.
Press DMS FWD/AFT SHORT to adjust zoom level.
Press TMS FWD SHORT to track the target - toggles between AREA TRACK (static) and POINT TRACK (moving).
Press TMS FWD LONG to designate the TGP's target as the SPI.
Press China Hat FWD LONG to slave all sensors to the SPI.
Press and hold the Nosewheel Steering Button to fire the laser.

tgp_slave_to_steerpoint.action: Verify the TGP is powered and set to A-G mode.
Set the AAP (Auxiliary Avionics Panel) Steerpoint Selector to MISSION.
Set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to STEER.
On the UFC, use the STEER rocker to select the desired steerpoint.
Press TMS AFT LONG to set the selected steerpoint as the SPI.
Press China Hat AFT LONG to slave the TGP to the steerpoint.
Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TGP feed to set the TGP as SOI.
Use the Slew Control Switch to put the TGP reticle on the target - same designation procedure as the TGP Start-Up & Lasing checklist above.
To make the TGP's own reticle the SPI instead, press TMS FWD LONG.

tgp_boresight.action: In the TGP page, press the OSB next to B-S (Boresight Function) - the pod points 150 mils (default) below the aircraft's zero sight line, directly forward.
To use a custom depression angle instead: a) enter the desired depression (in mils) on the UFC scratchpad, b) press the OSB next to B-S again.

tgp_laser_spot_search.action: Confirm the laser code the friendly asset (JTAC or another aircraft) is using, and that they're actively lasing before you try to track it.
Power up the TGP and set A-G mode (see the TGP Start-Up & Lasing checklist above).
Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TGP feed to set the TGP as SOI.
Press the OSB next to CNTL to enter the TGP A-G Control Page.
Enter the laser code to search for on the UFC scratchpad.
Press the OSB next to "LSS" (Laser Spot Search Code) to apply it.
Press the OSB next to RTN to return to the main TGP page.
Use the Slew Control Switch to point the TGP toward the JTAC's general location - it needs to be looking reasonably close to find the laser.
Press the OSB next to "LSS" to start the search (shortcut: China Hat AFT SHORT).
"LSRCH" appears while the TGP searches; the Situational Awareness Cue shows where it's scanning.
Once a laser reflection is detected, "DETECT" replaces "LSRCH" and the OSB changes from LSS to LST (Laser Spot Track) - the TGP automatically slews onto it.
After about 1 second, "DETECT" becomes "LTRACK" and a tracking-gate box appears over the laser spot.
The TGP diamond marks the Laser Spot Track (LST) on both the HUD and the TAD.
To exit LSS/LST mode, press the OSB next to LSS again.

If the JTAC sends you a 9-line or other tasking, a NEW TASKING message appears: a) open the MSG page to read it, b) press the OSB next to ACK (or TMS LEFT SHORT) to acknowledge/clear it, c) return to the TGP page.

tgp_laser_pointer_marker.action: Power up the TGP and set A-G mode.
Set MASTER ARM and LASER ARM switches to ARM.
Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TGP feed to set the TGP as SOI.
Select IR (Infrared) as the Laser Designator Mode via its OSB.
Slew the TGP reticle onto the target.

Press and hold the Nosewheel Steering Button to fire the pointer - a flashing "P" (Infrared Pointer) shows it's active. Unlike the laser designator, this can't guide a weapon - it's an IR marker only visible on Night Vision Goggles, for pointing a target out to another aircraft.

hmcs_power_up_and_profiles.action: Power up the HMCS: set the HMCS Power Switch to ON. By default the HMD overlay only shows when you're looking away from the HUD - press DMS LEFT LONG to toggle the overlay on/off regardless.

The HMCS has 3 preset profiles you can edit from the STAT page's HMCS sub-menu (per symbol: ON/OFF/OCLD-occludable, plus an optional cutoff range in nm). To modify one: a) select STAT, b) select HMCS, c) select the profile (PRO1/2/3), d) use the SYMBOL arrows to pick the symbol to change, e) press OCLD/ON/OFF to set its visibility, f) optionally enter a cutoff range on the UFC scratchpad and press RANGE.
Recommended profile for an attack run: CROSSHAIR - ON, OWN SPI - ON, HDC - ON (occlude the rest to avoid cluttering the HUD).

To cycle between the 3 profiles: a) press Coolie Hat DOWN to set the HMCS as SOI (confirm the SOI asterisk on the HMD), b) press DMS RIGHT SHORT to cycle profiles - or select one directly from the HMCS Symbology page.

hmcs_hook_symbol.action: Press Coolie Hat DOWN to set the HMCS as SOI (confirm the SOI asterisk).
Move your helmet to place the HMD crosshair over the symbol you want to hook.
Press TMS FWD SHORT to hook the symbol.
Hooked symbol data (bearing, distance, elevation, unit type) shows in the lower-left of the HMD.
A dashed box appears over the symbol with a yellow line to the crosshair.
Press TMS AFT SHORT to un-hook it.

hmcs_create_spi.action: Method 1 - on a hooked symbol: hook a symbol (see HMCS Hook Symbol above), then press TMS FWD LONG to create a SPI on it. Press TMS AFT SHORT to un-hook, or TMS AFT LONG to reset the SPI to the selected steerpoint without un-hooking.

Method 2 - with the HDC (Helmet Designation Cursor): a) press Coolie Hat DOWN to set the HMCS as SOI, b) press China Hat AFT SHORT to recage the HDC to the crosshair, c) move your helmet near the target, d) use the Slew Control Switch to walk the ground-stabilized HDC onto the target, e) press TMS FWD LONG to create a SPI on the HDC.

hmcs_slave_tgp_to_los.action: Power up the TGP and set it to A-G mode.
Press Coolie Hat DOWN to set the HMCS as SOI.
Press China Hat AFT SHORT to recage the HDC to the crosshair.
Move your helmet near the target.
Use the Slew Control Switch to walk the ground-stabilized HDC onto the target.
Press TMS FWD LONG to create a SPI on the HDC.
Press DMS LEFT SHORT to show a TGP feed repeater on the HMD.
Press DMS RIGHT LONG to slave the TGP to the HMCS line-of-sight (the SPI you just created) - the TGP's field-of-view box appears once slaved.
Cycle video mode with the Boat Switch (FWD = FLIR Black Hot, MIDDLE = CCD, AFT = FLIR White Hot).
To slew the TGP directly instead, press Coolie Hat LONG toward the TGP's MFCD to make it SOI, then use the Slew Control Switch and the TGP's own HOTAS controls.

hmcs_markpoint_creation.action: Press Coolie Hat DOWN to set the HMCS as SOI.
Press China Hat AFT SHORT to recage the HDC to the crosshair.
Move your helmet near the target.
Use the Slew Control Switch to walk the ground-stabilized HDC onto the target.
Press TMS RIGHT SHORT to create a markpoint on the HDC.
Optional: press TMS RIGHT LONG to make that markpoint the SPI.

sadl_network_setup.action: On the TAD page, press the OSB next to NET.
Your current GRP ID and OWN ID are shown on the right.
To set your Group ID: enter the number on the UFC scratchpad, then press the OSB next to GRP ID.
To set your Own ID: enter the number on the UFC scratchpad, then press the OSB next to OWN ID - you'll get an error if that number is already taken by someone else on the network.
Optional: type a callsign on the CDU keypad (e.g. FAC1), then press the OSB next to CALL.

sadl_hook_symbol.action: Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TAD to set it as SOI.
Use the Slew Control Switch to move the TAD cursor onto the symbol you want to hook - the SPI, TGP diamond, a waypoint/steerpoint, or the bullseye.
Press TMS FWD SHORT to hook it.
Hooked symbol data (bearing, distance, elevation) appears in the lower-right of the TAD.
Select the desired Hook Mode with its OSB - it sets which two points the hook line is drawn between (OWN/BULL/CURS/HOOK).
Press TMS AFT SHORT to un-hook.
Press China Hat AFT SHORT to reset the TAD cursor position.
With a symbol hooked, press TMS FWD LONG to make it the SPI - the HUD will then track that contact.

sadl_send_message.action: Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TAD to set it as SOI.
Slew the TAD cursor onto the wingman you want to message - their TN number (Own ID + Group ID) appears.
On the UFC scratchpad, type the wingman's TN number (e.g. 0201).
Press the OSB next to TO to set the recipient.
Type the message content on the CDU keypad.
Select MOD TEXT to enter the text.
Use the SET LINE OSBs to choose which line of text you're sending.

sadl_receive_message.action: A NEW MSG indication means a new message has arrived.
The message is displayed, along with the sender's TN number.

sadl_broadcast_spi.action: First create a SPI with any sensor - for example, with the TGP: a) power it up and select the TGP page in A-G mode, b) press Coolie Hat LONG toward its MFCD to set it as SOI, c) slew the reticle onto the target, d) press TMS FWD SHORT to track it, e) press TMS FWD LONG to designate it as the SPI.
Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TAD to set it as SOI.
You can broadcast to the whole SADL network or to one specific aircraft.
To send to one aircraft: a) slew the TAD cursor onto that aircraft, b) press SEND.
To broadcast to the whole network instead, press TMS LEFT LONG.
An "SPI ON" indication confirms your SPI is being broadcast - every member of the network then sees it on their own TAD as a Mini-SPI.

sadl_use_received_spi.action: A SPI received via SADL from a wingman appears as a "Mini-SPI" symbol (a two-tier wedding-cake shape).
Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TAD to set it as SOI.
Slew the TAD cursor onto the Mini-SPI symbol.
Press TMS FWD SHORT to hook it.
Press TMS FWD LONG to create your own SPI from it.
Press China Hat FWD LONG to slave all your sensors (TGP, Maverick, etc.) to that new SPI.

sadl_task_target.action: First create a SPI with any sensor - for example, with the TGP: a) power it up and select the TGP page in A-G mode, b) press Coolie Hat LONG toward its MFCD to set it as SOI, c) slew the reticle onto the target, d) press TMS FWD SHORT to track it, e) press TMS FWD LONG to designate it as the SPI.
Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TAD to set it as SOI.
Slew the TAD cursor onto the aircraft you want to task.
Press TMS FWD SHORT to hook it.
The hooked aircraft's network ID (Own ID - Group ID) appears below the SEND label.
Press the OSB next to SEND to send the target assignment.
Your wingman gets a NEW TASKING message on both MFCDs, and a red triangle appears on their TAD at the target's location.

sadl_receive_jtac_tasking.action: A NEW TASKING message appears on both MFCDs, regardless of the current page.
Press TMS LEFT SHORT to clear the message.
Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TAD to set it as SOI.
A red triangle marks the target on the TAD; a green X marks friendly units on the ground.
The full tasking (a digital 9-line) can be read on the MSG page.
Press WILCO to accept the tasking, or CNTCO to decline it.
Slew the TAD cursor onto the target symbol.
Press TMS FWD SHORT to hook it.
Once hooked, a CNC (Cancel) option becomes available.
Bearing and distance to the target are shown on the TAD.
Press TMS FWD LONG to make the hooked target your SPI.
Press China Hat FWD LONG to slave all sensors (HUD, TGP, Maverick) to that SPI.
Employ weapons as normal - see this file's own Weapons list.

radio_arc210_manual_frequency.action: Set the Radio Operation Mode Selector to TR (Transmit-Receive).
Set the Radio Frequency Mode Dial to MAN (Manual Frequency).
Set the SQL (Squelch) knob to ON.
Select the frequency: a) turn the manual frequency tuning knobs, or b) enter it on the UFC (e.g. "1330" for 133.000 MHz) and press the COM1 button.
Select AM or FM band with the AM/FM button.
The selected frequency shows on both the radio panel and the HUD's V1 field.
Transmit with the Microphone Switch FWD.

radio_arc210_preset_channel.action: Set the Radio Operation Mode Selector to TR.
Set the Radio Frequency Mode Dial to PRST (Preset Channel).
Set the SQL knob to ON.
Select the channel: a) turn the CHANNEL knob, or b) enter the channel number on the UFC and press COM1.
The selected channel shows on both the radio panel and the HUD's V1 field.
Transmit with the Microphone Switch FWD.

radio_arc210_edit_preset.action: Set the Radio Operation Mode Selector to CHG PRST (Change Preset).
Set the Radio Frequency Mode Dial to PRST (Preset Channel).
Select the channel to edit (e.g. Channel 4): turn the CHANNEL knob, or enter the number on the UFC and press COM1.
Decide the frequency to set for that channel (e.g. 256.000 MHz) - there are two ways to enter it, below.
Method 1, from the radio panel: turn the manual frequency tuning knobs to the target frequency.

Method 2, from the COMM page: a) press the OSB next to COMM, then ARC210 PRESETS, b) use the ROW arrows to select the channel, c) type the frequency on the UFC keypad (e.g. "2560" for 256.000 MHz), d) press the OSB next to FREQ to apply it, e) optionally type a name on the CDU keypad and press the OSB next to NAME.
Select AM or FM band with the AM/FM button.
Set the Radio Operation Mode Selector back to TR when done.

radio_arc186_vhf_fm.action: This is the VHF FM #2 radio (30.000-76.000 MHz), used to talk to JTAC units.
Set the Radio Frequency Mode to TR.
Adjust the radio volume as needed.
Set the Radio Function Selector to MAN (Manual Frequency) or PRE (Preset Channel).
Set the frequency with the Frequency Dials, or select the preset channel.
Transmit with the Microphone Switch AFT.

radio_arc164_uhf.action: This is the UHF radio (225.000-399.975 MHz) - normally what you'll use to talk to your flight.
Set the Radio Function Selector to MAIN or BOTH.
Adjust the radio volume as needed.
Set the Radio Frequency Mode Selector to MNL (Manual) or PRESET.
Set the frequency with the Frequency Dials, or select the preset channel.
Transmit with the Microphone Switch DOWN.
To save a frequency onto a preset channel: a) dial in the frequency, b) select the destination preset channel, c) press the LOAD button (under its cover).

air_to_air_refueling.action: Read your mission briefing for the tanker's TACAN channel and radio frequency.
Set your TACAN to A/A T/R and to the tanker's TACAN channel.
On the NMSP (Navigation Mode Select Panel), press TCN to slave the HSI to the TACAN beacon.

Contact the tanker on the frequency given in your mission briefing. Note: the guide's own instructions here specify the Legacy A-10C's VHF AM #1 radio, which is not installed on the Tank Killer variant this file is for (see the Radio system overview note) - the guide never says what covers tanker comms on Tank Killer instead, and this hasn't been verified in-game. Confirm the right radio yourself in DCS, then this step can be corrected with the real answer.
Press the Mic Switch FWD and contact the tanker (F6 radio menu).
Select "Intent to refuel" - the tanker gives you a rendezvous altitude, usually 20,000 or 10,000 ft.
Use the HSI to line up with the tanker - the needle marked "1" points toward it, with distance shown alongside.
Once close enough, call the tanker to begin pre-contact - if you're not lined up properly they'll tell you to "Return"; if you are, you're cleared to approach.
Make sure you're perfectly trimmed before starting the approach.
Set all weapon systems to SAFE.
Fly formation with the tanker itself, not the boom.
Confirm the READY light is illuminated.
Once contact is made you'll get a LATCHED notice - use the tanker's engines as a visual reference to hold position.

If you disconnect prematurely (it will happen), press the Nosewheel Steering Button to reset your fuel trap door - otherwise the boom operator can't make contact again (the light just shows READY once more).
Refueling is complete once the DISCONNECT light illuminates.
Close the fuel trap door and resume flight.

waypoint_designate_steerpoint.action: Set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to MISSION (gives access to every waypoint in the current mission).
Set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to STEER.
Press Coolie Hat UP to set the HUD as the Sensor of Interest (SOI).
Select the waypoint to use as your steerpoint - three ways: a) DMS UP/DOWN while the HUD is SOI cycles through waypoints, b) the CDU's own STEER switch or +/- rocker, c) the UFC's STEER rocker.
The selected waypoint shows as your steerpoint on both the HUD and CDU.

waypoint_navigate_to_steerpoint.action: Once a steerpoint is designated, cycle Master Mode to NAV.
Select STR PT navigation mode on the NMSP.
If the SPI isn't already set to STPT (steerpoint), press TMS AFT LONG with the HUD as SOI to set it.
Follow the steering cues on the HSI and HUD - the TVV points toward the steerpoint once STPT is the SPI.

waypoint_consult_data.action: Set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to MISSION.

To check a specific waypoint: set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to WAYPT, enter its number on the keypad, then press the LSK next to the Waypoint Number field - this opens the WP INFO page (name, heading/distance/time-to-go).
For more detail on that waypoint, press the LSK next to WAYPOINT, then use the Page Increment/Decrement rocker to flip between its two data pages (coordinates, elevation, wind).

To check the current steerpoint instead of one specific waypoint: set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to STEER - this opens the STEERPOINT INFO page (desired heading, distance, elevation, required airspeed, bearing/radial to it).
Other useful AAP CDU Selector positions: OTHER (unlocks the CDU's Function Select Keys, needed to add/edit anything) and POSITION (shows your own current position).

waypoint_add.action: Method 1 - copy an existing point: a) set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to MISSION, b) set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to OTHER, c) press the WP FSK, d) select the WAYPOINT branch, e) select "Copy to available mission point" - this copies the point (e.g. a hooked TAD symbol) into the next free mission-point slot.

Method 2 - enter coordinates manually: a) follow steps a-d above, b) select the desired coordinate format (L/L for Latitude/Longitude, or UTM/MGRS), c) enter the latitude on the keypad and press the LSK next to the latitude field, d) enter the longitude and press its LSK, e) enter the elevation (ft) and press its LSK, f) enter a unique name and press its LSK - the waypoint is created once every field is set. Coordinates are entered as one digit string per field (e.g. a latitude of 37°13.133'N is typed as 3713133).

waypoint_edit.action: Set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to MISSION.
Set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to OTHER.
Select the waypoint to edit: enter its number on the keypad, then press the LSK next to the Waypoint Number field.

Edit its latitude, longitude, and elevation the same way as adding a new waypoint (enter the value on the keypad, then press each field's own LSK) - see the Add Waypoints checklist for the coordinate entry format.

waypoint_offset.action: Use this when a target is given relative to an existing waypoint (e.g. "0.84 nm at a magnetic heading of 346 degrees from Waypoint 1") rather than as its own coordinates.
Set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to MISSION.
Set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to OTHER.
Enter the reference waypoint's number on the keypad and press the LSK next to the Waypoint Number field.

Enter the magnetic heading and distance offset on the keypad, then press the LSK next to MH/DIS. Format: HHHDD.T under 100 nm, HHHDDD.T from 100-999 nm, HHHDDDD.T at 1000+ nm (e.g. a heading of 346 and 0.8 nm is entered as 34600.8).
Type a name for the new offset waypoint on the keypad.
Select "Copy to available mission point" to save it into a free mission-point slot - it can then be selected like any other waypoint.

markpoint_navigate.action: Set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to MARK.
Set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to OTHER.
Press Coolie Hat UP to set the HUD as SOI.

Select the markpoint to use as your steerpoint - same three methods as designating a waypoint steerpoint (DMS UP/DOWN, the CDU STEER switch, or the UFC STEER rocker) - see the Waypoint Designate Steerpoint checklist.
The selected markpoint shows as your steerpoint on the HUD and CDU.
Select STR PT navigation mode on the NMSP.
If the SPI isn't already set to STPT, press TMS AFT LONG with the HUD as SOI.
Follow the steering cues on the HSI and HUD.

markpoint_consult_data.action: Set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to MARK.
Set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to OTHER.

Select the markpoint to view: enter its letter on the keypad and press the LSK next to the Waypoint Number field, or cycle through them with the +/- rocker - this shows its name, coordinates, elevation, and wind.

markpoint_add.action: Overhead method: pressing the MK button on the CDU creates a new markpoint at your current position - each press creates the next one in order (A-Y; Z is reserved for automatic weapon-release markpoints).
Designation method: point any sensor (HUD TDC, TGP, Maverick seeker, or TAD cursor) at the target, then press TMS RIGHT SHORT - each press creates the next markpoint in order (A-Y).
Weapon-release method: a Z markpoint is created automatically every time you release a weapon - each new release replaces the previous one.

HMCS method (Tank Killer): a) turn on HMCS power, b) press Coolie Hat DOWN to set the HMCS as SOI, c) press China Hat AFT SHORT to recage the HDC to the crosshair, d) move your helmet to place the crosshair near the target, e) use the Slew Control Switch to walk the ground-stabilized HDC onto it, f) press TMS RIGHT SHORT to create the markpoint, g) optionally press TMS RIGHT LONG to make it the SPI.
To browse your markpoints afterward, set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to MARK.

flight_plan_create.action: Set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to FLT PLAN (needed for the route to actually draw on the TAD).
Set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to OTHER.
Press the FPM (Flight Plan Menu) FSK.
Type a name for the new flight plan on the CDU keyboard, then press the LSK next to NEW FP.
Press the LSK next to FPBUILD [name] to open the Flight Plan Build page - it lists every waypoint in the plan (index 01 is always your Init Posit).
Add waypoints one at a time: enter a waypoint's number on the CDU keyboard, then press the LSK next to the sequence slot you want it in (01, 02, 03...).
Use the Page Increment/Decrement rocker to move to the next page once you've filled a page's worth of slots, and keep adding waypoints the same way - a flight plan can hold up to 40.

flight_plan_use.action: Set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to FLT PLAN.
Set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to OTHER.
Press the FPM (Flight Plan Menu) FSK.
Press the LSK next to the flight plan you want active - an asterisk marks it as selected.
Press the LSK next to your active flight plan again to toggle AUTO (advances to the next waypoint automatically once you're close enough) or MAN (you advance manually) sequencing.
The TAD now draws the flight plan's waypoints connected by green lines, and cycling the steerpoint switch moves through them in sequence.

divert_to_nearest_airfield.action: Set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to OTHER.
Press Coolie Hat UP to set the HUD as SOI.
On the UFC, press FUNC then 2 (NAV functions).
Press the OSB to select the DIVERT menu.
The Divert menu lists the closest airfields, with heading, distance, and time-to-go to each.
Select an airfield's OSB for its FLDINFO (Field Information) page - runway heading/elevation/length, ILS frequency (if any), TACAN channel (if any), and tower radio frequency.
The selected airfield becomes your current steerpoint, and the HUD shows the way there.
With the HUD still SOI, use DMS UP/DOWN SHORT to cycle through the other listed airfields.

adf_navigation.action: On the NMSP, make sure ILS and TCN are not selected.
Set the UHF radio's mode to ADF.
Set the UHF frequency mode to MNL (Manual).
Dial in the beacon's frequency, from your mission briefing/kneeboard.
Confirm signal with the UHF HOMING light illuminated.
On the HSI, follow Bearing Pointer 1 toward the beacon - ADF gives bearing only, no range.

tacan_navigation.action: Power up the TACAN panel: set the Mode Selector to T/R (Transmit-Receive).
Set the station's TACAN channel on the panel (the right knob sets X/Y, the two left/right selector knobs set the channel number).
On the NMSP, press TCN to slave the HSI to the TACAN beacon.
Set the desired course to the station with the HSI Course Set Knob.
After a few seconds, the HSI shows DME (distance) to the station in nautical miles.
Steer to center the TACAN CDI - the deviation from centerline shrinks as you approach the radial.
The pointed end of the Course Arrow and Bearing Pointer 1 both indicate the beacon's direction.
A centered CDI means you're established on your selected radial.
Turn to follow Bearing Pointer 1 (or the course needle) along that radial to the station.

anchor_point_bullseye_setup.action: Set the AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob to MISSION.
Set the AAP CDU Selector Knob to WAYPT - this opens the WP INFO page.
Enter the number of the waypoint you want to use as the new anchor point on the keypad, then press the LSK next to the Waypoint Number field.
Press the LSK next to HUD OFF to also show anchor point/bullseye data on the HUD.
Select ANCHR mode on the NMSP.
The anchor point is now set - check it on the CDU, HUD, HSI, and TAD.
You could also create a brand-new waypoint (rather than reusing an existing one) and set that as the anchor point instead - the process is the same either way.

ils_landing_approach.action: Set your VHF radio to TR, manual frequency, and the tower's briefed frequency - call in for an inbound request.
Enter the ILS frequency for your destination runway - find it on the airfield's FLDINFO page via the Divert function, or from your kneeboard.
Set your HSI course to the runway's magnetic heading.
On the NMSP, set homing mode to ILS and turn toward the runway.
Align with the runway using the HSI, CDI, and the ADI's localizer steering bar.
Inside about 10 nm, the Glide Slope Fail flag disappears and gives vertical guidance for a 3-degree glide slope.
Fly the glide slope by keeping the Glide Slope Steering Bar and Deviation Indicator centered, alongside the localizer bar.

Once both the localizer and glide slope are captured, deploy the landing gear, flaps, and airbrakes and continue as in the standard landing checklist (radar altitude reference, -500 ft/min descent, touchdown - no flare needed).

weapons.name: MK-82 Low-Drag Unguided Bomb
weapons.employment_notes: 500 lb unguided general-purpose bomb, CCIP dive-bombing. Two release techniques share the same DSMS profile setup: manual CCIP (you release) and CCIP-CR/Computer Release (aircraft auto-releases when in solution, letting you start your escape maneuver earlier). Reference: Part 10, section 2.1.

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP).

switchology: Select the DSMS (Digital Stores Management System) page.
Select the MK-82 Bomb (turns green when selected).
Select the PROF (Weapon Profile) menu.
Set CCIP mode.
Set Release Type: SGL (single), PRS (pairs), RIP SGL (each press releases the RIP QTY setting), or RIP PRS (each press releases the RIP PRS quantity, in pairs).
Set Bomb Fuze Setting (Nose, Tail, or Nose & Tail).
Optional: set Bomb Ripple Quantity and Bomb Interval Distance (ft) via the UFC scratchpad and the RIP QTY / FT OSBs.

Optional: set horizontal/vertical offset (-15 to +15 mils), eject velocity (-10 to +30 ft/sec), rack delay (-0.40 to +0.40), Escape Maneuver Type (NONE/CLB/TRN/TLT), Time of Fall, and Minimum Release Altitude HUD cue - all via the UFC scratchpad and their respective OSBs.
Press the OSB next to SAVE to save the weapon profile.

switchology.text: Select the MK-82 profile via the Option Select Buttons, then press the OSB next to ACT PRO (Active Profile). While HUD is SOI, you can also cycle profiles/stations with the DMS switch left/right.

switchology: Set the IFFCC switch to TEST (middle position).
For manual CCIP release: select CCIP CONSENT with the SEL rocker key and cycle with DATA until it shows OFF.
For CCIP-CR (auto) release instead: select CCIP CONSENT and cycle with DATA until it shows 3/9 (solution cue must pass through the reticle) or 5 MIL (solution cue must pass over the reticle pipper).
Set the IFFCC switch back to ON (UP) - the HUD returns to normal.

switchology.text: Press the Master Mode button until CCIP HUD mode is selected.
Press Coolie Hat UP (short) to set the HUD as SOI (an asterisk indicates HUD is SOI).

switchology: Verify the HUD shows MAN REL mode, CCIP release, the MK-82 profile, and ARM status.
Perform a shallow dive between 10-45 degrees from at least 10,000 ft.

switchology.text: Manual CCIP: a dashed 'Out of Solution' PBIL appears when not yet close enough; when close enough the CCIP Bombing Reticle appears and the PBIL turns solid. Place the reticle center on the target and press and hold the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) to release.

CCIP-CR (auto): once pitched down more than 3 degrees, maneuver to place the designation pipper on the target and press and HOLD the Weapon Release Button. The PBIL turns solid and an Azimuth Steering Line (ASL) appears with a Solution Cue and Time-To-Release Numeric (TTRN). Keep flying the Solution Cue down the ASL - with the button still held, bombs release automatically once the Solution Cue passes through the reticle/pipper.

weapons.name: MK-82AIR High-Drag Unguided Bomb
weapons.employment_notes: 500 lb high-drag (retarded) bomb for low-altitude release, CCRP level-release mode. The SPI (target aim point) can be designated either with the HUD TDC or with the Targeting Pod. Reference: Part 10, section 2.2.

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP). Select the DSMS page, select MK-82AIR Bomb (green when selected), select the PROF menu.

switchology: Set CCRP mode. Set Release Type (SGL/PRS/RIP SGL/RIP PRS, same options as the MK-82).
Set Bomb Fuze Setting: nose fuze only = 'slick' (ballute not deployed); nose/tail or tail fuze = 'retarded' (ballute deployed).
Optional: ripple quantity/interval, offsets, eject velocity, rack delay, Escape Maneuver Type, HD/LD Time of Fall, Minimum Release Altitude cue - same UFC-scratchpad-plus-OSB pattern as the MK-82.
Press the OSB next to SAVE to save the profile, then select the MK-82APO profile and press ACT PRO to activate it.

switchology.text: Option 1 - designate SPI with the HUD TDC: press Master Mode button for CCRP, Coolie Hat UP to set HUD as SOI, verify 5 MIL/CCIP release/MK-82APO/ARM on the HUD, use the Slew Control Switch to move the TDC (caged on the velocity vector by default) onto the target, then press TMS FWD LONG to set that TDC location as the SPI.

Option 2 - designate SPI with the Targeting Pod: press Master Mode for CCRP, set TGP switch ON on the AHCP, press the OSB next to TGP and select A-G mode, press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the TGP feed to set TGP as SOI, then designate the target with the TGP (video mode via Boat Switch, FOV via China Hat, slew reticle onto target, TMS FWD SHORT to track, TMS FWD LONG to designate as SPI, China Hat FWD LONG to slave all sensors to the SPI).

switchology: Fly level and align the CCRP Projected Bomb Release Line (PBRL)/pipper with the Azimuth Steering Line (ASL).

switchology.text: At about 6 seconds on the TTRN, the Solution Cue starts falling down the ASL - press and hold the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) and maneuver so the Solution Cue falls through the CCRP pipper.

switchology: Bombs release automatically once the Solution Cue passes through the pipper.

weapons.name: MK-84 Low-Drag Unguided Bomb
weapons.employment_notes: 2,000 lb-class unguided general-purpose bomb. The guide has no separate MK-84 walkthrough - its Unguided Ordnance Usage quick-reference chart (end of the weapons chapter) covers the MK-82, MK-82AIR, MK-84, CBU-87 and CBU-97 together, so the MK-84 uses the same three release modes as the MK-82 (manual CCIP, CCIP-CR, CCRP) with the same DSMS profile options. For the full MK-82 profile detail (ripple, offsets, escape maneuvers, time of fall) see the MK-82 entry. Reference: Part 10, section 2.1 and the Unguided Ordnance Usage chart.
switchology: On the DSMS page select the MK-84 Bomb (turns green), open PROF, choose the delivery mode you plan to use (CCIP or CCRP) and the Release Type (SGL, PRS, RIP SGL or RIP PRS), plus the Bomb Fuze Setting (Nose, Tail, or Nose & Tail) and any optional settings (ripple quantity/interval, Minimum Release Altitude cue, etc. - same options as the MK-82), then press SAVE, select the profile and press ACT PRO.

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP).
Press Coolie Hat UP (short) to set the HUD as SOI, then use DMS LEFT/RIGHT to cycle to the bomb and profile you want.

switchology: Choose the consent-to-release behavior in the IFFCC TEST menu (IFFCC switch to TEST, SEL to CCIP CONSENT, cycle with DATA): OFF = manual release (MAN REL - the weapon leaves the moment you press), 3/9 = the Solution Cue must pass through the reticle, 5 MIL = the Solution Cue must pass over the reticle pipper. Use OFF for manual CCIP and 3/9 or 5 MIL for CCIP-CR. Entering the TEST menu resets the HUD master mode to GUNS, so set the IFFCC back to ON afterward and then pick your master mode.

switchology.text: CCIP (manual release): press Master Mode until CCIP is selected (MAN REL shows in the HUD). Optionally make the target the SPI first (TGP, HUD TDC, etc.) - the bottom-left of the HUD shows which sensor it came from.

switchology: CCIP works best when started from above 10,000 ft: pitch nose-down 30-40 degrees and line the Projected Bomb Impact Line (PBIL) up with the target - dashed while the reticle is below the HUD field of view, solid once you can see the reticle.

switchology.text: Press the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) when the reticle is over the target - keep the reticle below the Min Range Staple on the line.

weapons.name: M-151 Hydra 70 Rockets
weapons.employment_notes: 2.75in unguided rockets, CCIP dive-fire. Reference: Part 10, section 2.3. switchology: Set CCIP mode. Set Release Type (SGL/PRS/RIP SGL/RIP PRS - same meanings as bombs, but launching rockets instead of dropping bombs).

switchology.text: Press Master Mode button until CCIP HUD mode is selected; press Coolie Hat UP (short) to set HUD as SOI; verify MAN REL/CCIP/M-151/ARM on the HUD.

switchology: Perform a shallow dive between 10-45 degrees from at least 10,000 ft.
A CCIP Rocket Reticle & Pipper appears when not close enough; inside 2 nm slant range the numeric range readout is replaced by an unwinding analog range bar. Place the reticle center on the target.

switchology.text: At a slant range of around 1 nm, hold down the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) to launch rockets.

An Azimuth Steering Line (ASL) appears in the HUD with a Solution Cue circle near the top, and the rocket pipper shows with no range indicators. Fly the rocket pipper inside the Solution Cue, then press the Weapon Release Button.

weapons.name: GAU-8/A 30mm Gun (Air-to-Ground)
weapons.employment_notes: 7-barrel Gatling cannon, the A-10's signature weapon. Four gunsight reticle modes are cyclable with DMS while HUD is SOI: CCIP Reticle (most accurate), CCIP Cross (simplified, nearly as accurate), 4/8/12 Reticle, and 4000ft Wind-Corrected Cross (both useful as fallbacks when a CCIP solution can't be computed, i.e. a CCIP INVALID HUD message because the target is higher than the aircraft). Reference: Part 10, section 2.4. Range guidance from the guide's Guns quick-reference chart: the gun is best used from 0.5 to 2 miles slant range - stay at 0.5-0.8 miles (ideally from behind) against tanks, about 1.2 miles for lightly armored targets, and about 1.5 miles for unarmored ones. switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP). Set GUN/PAC (Precision Attitude Correction) Switch - ARM (UP). Confirm GUN READY indication is visible.

switchology: To use PAC, make sure EAC (Enhanced Attitude Control) and the PITCH/YAW SAS switches are ON.

switchology.text: Press the Master Mode button until GUNS HUD mode is selected; press Coolie Hat UP (short) to set HUD as SOI.

CCIP Reticle / CCIP Cross: the moving-target lead indices assume a 20kt perpendicular target - place the target between the pipper and the indices if it's moving. Put the target under the reticle/cross, partially depress the trigger (first detent) to activate PAC and stabilize flight, wait until slant range is 0.7 nm, then depress the trigger (second detent) for a short 1-second burst.

4000ft Wind Corrected Cross: also for above-altitude targets when CCIP is unavailable. Put the target under the cross, partially depress the trigger to activate PAC, then depress the trigger (second detent) when in range for a short burst.

weapons.name: GBU-38 JDAM (JTAC Coordinates)

9-line reference: Line 1 IP/BP, Line 2 heading from IP to target, Line 3 distance IP/BP to target, Line 4 target elevation (MSL), Line 5 target description, Line 6 target grid coordinates, Line 7 target mark type, Line 8 location of friendlies, Line 9 egress direction - plus remarks (troops in contact, danger close, SEAD, hazards, requested ordnance).
If the JTAC says 'Standby Data', a new tasking arrives on the MSG page - press the OSB next to MSG to view it, and the OSB next to ACK to acknowledge/clear the caution.

Enter the target coordinates as a new waypoint in the CDU: set STEER PT selector to MISSION and PAGE selector to OTHER, select the WP function key, select LSK next to STEERPOINT, select LSK to create a new waypoint, select LSK next to L/L to toggle to UTM format, type the JTAC's coordinates on the CDU keypad and select the LSK to apply them, optionally type and apply a waypoint name.

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP), select DSMS page, select GBU-38 Bomb (green when selected), select PROF menu - CCRP is the only selectable mode.

switchology: Optional: set a Minimum Release Altitude HUD cue via the UFC scratchpad and MIN ALT OSB, then press the OSB next to SAVE.

switchology.text: Press Coolie Hat UP to set HUD as SOI, select the new JTAC waypoint with the STEER rocker or DMS up/down, and if it isn't already the SPI press TMS AFT LONG to set it as the SPI.

switchology.text: Press and hold the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) until the JDAM releases - it homes on the entered coordinates by itself via GPS.

weapons.name: GBU-38 JDAM (Targeting Pod)
weapons.employment_notes: Same GBU-38 JDAM, but the target point comes from the Targeting Pod (with laser ranging) instead of JTAC coordinates. Reference: Part 10, section 2.6.

switchology.text: Press and hold the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) until the JDAM releases - it homes on the markpoint via GPS.

weapons.name: CBU-103 Wind Corrected Munitions Dispenser
weapons.employment_notes: The CBU-87 cluster bomb fitted with a Wind Corrected Munition Dispenser (WCMD, 'Wick Mid') tail kit. Unlike the JDAMs it isn't GPS-guided - the tail kit uses the aircraft's inertial navigation data to know where it is and where the SPI is, then steers to it. Employment follows the guide's Guided Ordnance Usage chart (IAM section); the CBU-105 entry has the full Targeting Pod designation walkthrough, and everything there applies here apart from the HoF value and the extra RPM setting. Reference: Part 10, section 2.7 and the Guided Ordnance Usage chart.

weapons.name: CBU-105 Wind Corrected Munitions Dispenser

switchology: Set the HoF per station before flight: DSMS page - INV (Inventory) page - select the CBU-105 station - INV STAT - click the OSB next to HOF repeatedly until 2200 ft is set - OSB next to LOAD (or LOAD SYM for a symmetrical loadout on both pylons).
