switchology: Program the laser code the bomb will track, the same way as the GBU-12: DSMS - INV page - select the GBU-10 station - INV STAT - enter the code on the UFC scratchpad - OSB next to LSR CODE - OSB next to LOAD (or LOAD SYM for a symmetrical loadout).

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP). On the DSMS page select the GBU-10 Bomb, open PROF (CCRP), set the Release Type, Fuze Setting and Auto Laser / LS TIME as for the GBU-12, then SAVE and activate the profile (ACT PRO).
Press Coolie Hat UP (short) to set the HUD as SOI and use DMS LEFT/RIGHT to select the GBU-10 profile.

switchology: Plan to release above 5,000 ft so the bomb has time to correct (10,000-15,000 ft is ideal).
Make the target the SPI (TGP, HUD TDC or a Maverick seeker). In CCRP you never need to put the reticle over the target. The bottom-left of the HUD shows which sensor the SPI came from.

switchology.text: Press Master Mode until CCRP is selected. The guide's chart notes that laser-guided bombs in CCRP can only use the 3/9 consent-to-release mode (set in the IFFCC TEST menu). The bombing reticle only appears at more than 3 degrees of depression angle.

Unless Auto-Lase is set in the profile or someone else is lasing, fire the laser yourself: with TGP LATCH OFF press and hold the Nosewheel Steering Button; with LATCH ON press it once. A flashing L in the HUD confirms the laser is active (in every mode).

switchology: The upside-down bracket on the line is the minimum-range staple (set by your Minimum Altitude, Height of Function and fuze settings) - keep the CCRP reticle below it for a valid release.

switchology.text: Press and hold the Weapon Release Button while the Solution Cue passes through the reticle. An X over the cue means the steering error is too large or you're pitched down too much - the weapon won't release. In a ripple drop, the Desired Release Cue puts the middle bomb on the target (with an even number of bombs it brackets the target point).
Keep lasing until the bomb follows the laser to impact, then stop the laser.

weapons.name: GBU-12 Paveway II Laser-Guided Bomb
weapons.employment_notes: 500 lb laser-guided bomb - unlike the JDAM family it doesn't fly itself, and requires continuous laser designation (from your own TGP, in this workflow) through impact. Reference: Part 10, section 2.8. Guide note: normally you'd launch the GBU-12 first and then fire the laser to guide it in; the guide simplifies by lasing first, then attacking.
switchology: Program the laser code the bomb will track: DSMS - INV page - select the GBU-12 station - INV STAT - enter the desired code (e.g. 1687) on the UFC scratchpad - OSB next to LSR CODE - OSB next to LOAD (or LOAD SYM for a symmetrical loadout).

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP), select DSMS page, select GBU-12 Bomb, select PROF menu.

switchology: Set CCRP mode, Release Type (SGL/PRS/RIP SGL/RIP PRS), and Bomb Fuze Setting.
Set Auto Laser: OFF to fire the laser manually, or ON with an LS TIME (seconds before impact the laser fires automatically - 8 sec recommended for best accuracy, 0 defaults to 4 sec).

Optional: offsets, eject velocity, rack delay, Escape Maneuver Type, Time of Fall, Minimum Release Altitude cue, and Solution Option (ORP - Optimal Release Point, or BAL - ballistic) via UFC scratchpad + OSBs.
Press the OSB next to SAVE, then select the GBU-12 profile and press ACT PRO to activate it.

switchology.text: On the AHCP, set TGP switch ON and LASER ARM to ARM. Press the OSB next to TGP, select A-G mode, and press Coolie Hat LONG toward that MFCD to set TGP as SOI.

Designate the target with the TGP (Boat Switch for video mode, China Hat for FOV, slew reticle onto target, DMS to zoom, TMS FWD SHORT to track), then TMS FWD LONG to designate the TGP point as SPI, and China Hat FWD LONG to slave all sensors to the SPI. Press Master Mode until CCRP HUD mode is selected.

Enter the same laser code on the TGP AG Control Page (OSB next to CNTL, enter code, OSB next to 'L'), select LATCH mode (ON = laser stays firing once triggered), OSB next to RTN to return, then press the Nosewheel Steering Button to fire the laser.

Fly level and align the CCRP Projected Bomb Release Line with the ASL. At about 6 seconds on the TTRN the Solution Cue starts falling - press and hold the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) and maneuver so the cue falls through the CCRP pipper; the bomb releases automatically.

Verify the laser is firing (blinking 'L' on the HUD) - if not, press the Nosewheel Steering Button again. Keep lasing until the bomb follows the laser to impact, then press the Nosewheel Steering Button once more to stop firing.

weapons.name: AGM-65 Maverick (IR, Maverick Sensor Only)
weapons.employment_notes: Infrared-guided air-to-ground missile, locked using its own seeker rather than the Targeting Pod - shorter effective range but simpler to set up. Reference: Part 10, section 2.9.

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP), select the MAV page on an MFCD, press the OSB next to EO OFF to begin the ~3-minute Electro-Optical alignment (MAV page shows ALIGN, HUD shows ALN). Alignment is complete when ALIGN disappears and HUD shows RDY.
Select DSMS page and select the AGM-65 Missile (green when selected). While HUD is SOI, cycle stations/profiles with DMS left/right.
Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the MAV feed to set the Maverick as SOI.

switchology: Optional: set the Adjustment Boresight Function and/or missile slew rate (default 5.0; some pilots prefer 9.0) via the UFC scratchpad and SLEW OSB.

switchology.text: Lock the target: select video mode with the Boat Switch, FOV with the China Hat, use the Slew Control Switch to put the MAV reticle on the target - releasing the slew lets the seeker auto-lock onto the center of mass of whatever's inside the tracking gate (if it can't lock, the seeker enters Break Lock and the crosshairs expand). TMS AFT SHORT ground-stabilizes the reticle; TMS FWD LONG sets the Maverick as SPI.
When the missile has a good lock (generally 3-7 nm), press the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) to fire - a LAUNCH INHIBIT message means no valid lock yet.

switchology: Note: flaps must be UP when firing any missile, or they can be damaged by the launch.

weapons.name: AGM-65 Maverick (IR, Targeting Pod Slaved)
weapons.employment_notes: Same IR Maverick, but the Targeting Pod (longer range, easier to use) designates the target first and slaves the Maverick seeker to it, so the missile locks once in range. Reference: Part 10, section 2.10.
switchology: Prepare the Maverick: Master Arm ON, MAV page, OSB next to EO OFF to align (~3 min, watch for RDY), select the AGM-65 Missile on the DSMS page.

switchology.text: On the AHCP set TGP switch ON, press the OSB next to TGP and select A-G mode, then press Coolie Hat LONG toward that MFCD to set TGP as SOI.

Designate the target with the TGP (Boat Switch for video mode, China Hat for FOV, slew reticle onto target, DMS to zoom, TMS FWD SHORT to track), verify TGP is SOI, then press TMS FWD LONG to set it as the SPI.

Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MFCD showing the MAV feed to set the Maverick as SOI, then press China Hat FWD LONG to slave the Maverick seeker to the SPI - it slews there automatically (expect Break Lock crosshairs until it locks).
As you approach, use the DLZ (Dynamic Launch Zone) to judge range; once inside 3-7 nm press TMS FWD SHORT to attempt a lock (may take a couple of tries) - the crosshair symbology changes once locked.
When the missile has a good lock, press the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) to fire - LAUNCH INHIBIT means no valid lock yet. Flaps must be UP when firing.

weapons.name: AGM-65L Laser Maverick (Tank Killer Only)
weapons.employment_notes: Laser-guided Maverick variant, exclusive to the A-10C II Tank Killer. Tracks a specific laser code (PRF) rather than an IR image, so it can be cued onto a target lased by your own TGP, another aircraft, or a JTAC laser designator. Reference: Part 10, section 2.11.

switchology.text: Program the missile's laser code: either via DSMS - INV - select the AGM-65L station - INV STAT - enter code (e.g. 1687) on the UFC scratchpad - OSB next to CODE - OSB next to LOAD/LOAD SYM; or via the MAV page using the Boat Switch to cycle each of the 4 code digits (1-7) and, optionally, a 5th 'C' countermeasure-mode digit.
Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP), select DSMS page, select the AGM-65L Missile.
On the AHCP set TGP switch ON and LASER ARM to ARM. Press the OSB next to TGP, select A-G mode, press Coolie Hat LONG toward that MFCD to set TGP as SOI.
Designate the target with the TGP and press TMS FWD LONG to set it as the SPI.
Enter the same laser code on the TGP AG Control Page (OSB CNTL, enter code, OSB 'L'), choose LATCH mode, OSB RTN to return, then press the Nosewheel Steering Button to start lasing.

Press Coolie Hat LONG toward the MAV feed's MFCD to set the Maverick as SOI, then press TMS FWD SHORT to uncage the seeker into 'Activate' mode - it scans its boresight line of sight for the matching laser code; a flashing GPI (Gimbal Pointing Indicator) means it's detecting energy, a solid white square means a valid lock.

If no return is detected, releasing the slew switch enters 'Slew'/scan mode (GPI sweeps +/-22 degrees); alternatively, China Hat FWD LONG slaves the seeker to the current SPI/TGP point to auto-track-scan that area.

switchology: Verify the laser is firing (blinking 'L' on HUD) and the GPI shows a solid white square inside the Launch Constraint Circle.

switchology.text: When locked and in range (generally 3-7 nm, per the Maverick DLZ), press the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) to fire - the missile tracks the laser to impact. Press the Nosewheel Steering Button again after impact to stop lasing.

weapons.name: GBU-54 Laser JDAM (Tank Killer Only)
weapons.employment_notes: Hybrid of the GBU-38 JDAM and GBU-12 laser bomb, exclusive to the A-10C II Tank Killer - can guide on INS/GPS coordinates alone (launch-and-leave, works through cloud/dust) or switch to laser tracking, which automatically takes precedence if a matching laser code is detected. Useful for engaging moving targets designated by your own TGP, a wingman, or a JTAC laser. Reference: Part 10, section 2.12.
switchology: Program the laser code via DSMS - INV - select the GBU-54 station - INV STAT - enter code (e.g. 1687) - OSB next to CODE - OSB next to LOAD/LOAD SYM.

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP), select DSMS page, select GBU-54 Bomb, select PROF menu - CCRP is the only selectable mode.

switchology: Optional profile settings: AUTO LS (auto-fire the laser after launch) with an LS TIME, IMP AZ (impact azimuth), IMP ANG (impact angle), and Minimum Release Altitude cue - all via UFC scratchpad + OSB, then SAVE and activate the profile (ACT PRO).

switchology.text: On the AHCP set TGP switch ON and LASER ARM to ARM. Press the OSB next to TGP, select A-G mode, press Coolie Hat LONG toward that MFCD to set TGP as SOI.
Designate the target with the TGP, press TMS FWD LONG to set it as the SPI, and China Hat FWD LONG to slave all sensors to the SPI.

switchology: Enter the same laser code on the TGP AG Control Page (OSB CNTL, enter code, OSB 'L'), choose LATCH mode, OSB RTN to return.
Fly level and align the velocity vector (or CCRP reticle, Legacy) with the ASL; wait for the DLZ current-range caret to fall between max/min range, showing MAN REL.

switchology.text: Press and hold the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) until the GBU-54 releases - it homes on the GPS coordinates by default.

To switch to laser guidance instead, press the Nosewheel Steering Button to fire the laser - the bomb automatically switches to tracking it instead of INS/GPS. Press the Nosewheel Steering Button again after impact to stop lasing.

weapons.name: APKWS Laser-Guided Rockets (Tank Killer Only)
weapons.employment_notes: AGR-20A - a standard 2.75in Hydra 70 rocket fitted with a laser guidance kit and control fins, exclusive to the A-10C II Tank Killer. Comes in M-151 (High Explosive) or M-282 (Penetrator) warheads. Guided the same way as the laser Maverick/GBU-12/GBU-54: designate and lase with the TGP, fire in a CCIP dive like unguided rockets. Reference: Part 10, section 2.13.
switchology: Program the laser code via DSMS - INV - select the APKWS (M-151L/M-282L) station - INV STAT - enter code (e.g. 1687) - OSB next to CODE - OSB next to LOAD/LOAD SYM.

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP), select DSMS page, select the APKWS rockets, select PROF menu.

switchology: Set CCIP mode and Release Type (SGL/PRS/RIP SGL/RIP PRS), optional ripple quantity/offsets/Minimum Release Altitude cue, then SAVE and activate the profile (ACT PRO).

switchology.text: On the AHCP set TGP switch ON and LASER ARM to ARM. Press the OSB next to TGP, select A-G mode, press Coolie Hat LONG toward that MFCD to set TGP as SOI.
Designate the target with the TGP and press TMS FWD LONG to set it as the SPI.
Enter the same laser code on the TGP AG Control Page (OSB CNTL, enter code, OSB 'L'), choose LATCH mode, OSB RTN to return, then press the Nosewheel Steering Button to start lasing.
Press the Master Mode button until CCIP HUD mode is selected; verify MAN REL/CCIP/profile/ARM on the HUD.

switchology: Perform a shallow dive between 10-45 degrees from at least 10,000 ft. Verify the laser is firing (blinking 'L'). When slant range to target is under 10 nm, place the CCIP reticle center on the target.

switchology.text: At a slant range of about 5.0-5.5 nm, hold down the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) to launch - the rockets track the laser to impact. Press the Nosewheel Steering Button again after impact to stop lasing.

weapons.name: GAU-8/A 30mm Gun (Air-to-Air)
weapons.employment_notes: Same cannon used air-to-air via a lead-computing 'funnel' reticle sized to a target aircraft's wingspan. Several aircraft profiles are preset in the AAS (Air-to-Air Sub-menu); custom wingspan/length/speed profiles can also be programmed for aircraft without a preset. Reference: Part 10, sections 3.1 A and B.

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP), set GUN/PAC Switch to GUNARM (DOWN), confirm GUN READY.
Press Coolie Hat UP (short) to set HUD as SOI, then press and hold the Master Mode Switch for about 3 seconds to enter Air-to-Air Master Mode.
Use DMS LEFT/RIGHT to cycle the AAS aircraft options to match the target you're engaging.

Fly so the target sits inside the gun funnel with just its wingtips/rotor tips touching the funnel sides (or use the AMIL - Air Mass Impact Line - which shows the lead angle from trajectory shift and gravity drop over the first ~2 seconds of flight), then depress the trigger (second detent) for a short 1-second burst.

switchology: To program a custom funnel for an aircraft without a preset: set IFFCC to TEST, SEL to AAS then ENT, enable/disable which preset profiles show up via SEL+ENT ('o' = available); MAN-FXD is the programmable fixed-wing profile, MAN-RTY the rotary-wing one.

In the chosen MAN-FXD/MAN-RTY menu, set FXD WNGSPN (wingspan, ft), FXD LENGTH (ft), and FXD TGTSPEED (approx. target speed, kts) via the SEL/DATA rockers, then SEL to STORE and ENT, SEL to EXIT AAS and ENT, set IFFCC back to ON.

switchology.text: Select the new custom profile the same way as a preset: Coolie Hat UP for HUD SOI, hold Master Mode ~3 sec for Air-to-Air mode, DMS LEFT/RIGHT to select it.

weapons.name: AIM-9 Sidewinder
weapons.employment_notes: Infrared-guided air-to-air missile. Reference: Part 10, section 3.2. The guide's own note and its Air-to-Air quick-reference chart add the Targeting Pod's A-A mode and a few extra seeker controls (last three steps). The chart is an older revision (Rev 1.0.6) than the numbered procedure above, so treat any control that differs on your build as the newer one.

switchology.text: Set Master Arm Switch - ON (UP), select DSMS page, select the AIM-9 Missile (green when selected).
Press Coolie Hat UP (short) to set HUD as SOI, use DMS LEFT/RIGHT to select the desired weapon profile, then press and hold the Master Mode Switch ~3 seconds to enter Air-to-Air Master Mode.

The Sidewinder reticle is caged in boresight mode by default (steer the aircraft to keep it on the target) - press TMS FWD SHORT to uncage it so it actively searches for heat signatures (you'll hear a low-pitch growl); TMS AFT SHORT re-cages it. The Slew Control Switch can slew the reticle manually.

switchology: Once the seeker tracks a heat source, the reticle locks on and the growl becomes high-pitched.

switchology.text: Press the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) to fire.

Optional spotter: the TGP also works in Air-to-Air mode. It starts in A-A boresight; slew it with the Slew Control Switch (the view is space-stabilized). A small cross marks a trackable air target inside the narrow field of view, and the large crosshair opens while searching and closes once it detects a target. TMS FWD SHORT point-tracks it (POINT shows and a box is drawn around the target); TMS AFT breaks the track.

Extra seeker controls (chart): a second TMS FWD press while uncaged puts the seeker into a circular scan that starts tracking automatically once it sees enough IR signal; TMS AFT commands the missile back to boresight (break lock); China Hat FWD commands an uncaged-track if the missile is caged.

Missile reject / slave (chart): China Hat AFT once cages and boresights the missile; a second press rejects it and takes it out of service (if every missile in the profile is rejected they all return to active service). China Hat FWD LONG slaves the AIM-9 to the TGP line of sight.

ordnance_jettison.name: Selective Jettison
ordnance_jettison.notes: Drops a chosen station individually, with control over rack vs. store and fuze state. Reference: Part 10, section 4.1.
steps: Select the DSMS page and press the OSB next to SJET (Selective Jettison).
Select the desired station via its OSB - it flashes once selected.
Select Jettison Mode: RACK (jettisons the launcher rack and the store), STR (jettisons the store only, keeps the rack), or MSL (fires a Maverick without arming or guiding it).
If STR mode is selected, choose the Fuze Option: SAFE (disarmed), NOSE ARM, TAIL ARM, or ARMED (both nose and tail fuzes armed).

steps.text: Press the Weapon Release Button (RALT+SPACE) to drop the ordnance.

ordnance_jettison.name: Emergency Stores Jettison
ordnance_jettison.notes: One-button jettison of everything except the Targeting Pod and ECM pod, regardless of landing gear position. Reference: Part 10, section 4.2.
steps: Press the EXT STORES JETT (External Stores Jettison) button.
All stores on stations 1 through 11 (excluding the Targeting Pod and ECM pod) release in station-priority order, regardless of landing gear handle position.

systems_notes.notes: Written independently, not from the guide - standard AoA-indexer symbology: a chevron pointing down means fast (low AoA), a chevron pointing up means slow (high AoA), and a circle means on-speed. Only active with the nose gear down, so it's a landing-approach aid, not a general flight instrument.

SOI (Sensor of Interest) is whichever sensor you're currently controlling - the HUD, the TGP, a Maverick's seeker, or the HMCS. SPI (Sensor Point of Interest) is where that sensor is currently pointed/locked - SOI is picking which sensor you're holding, SPI is where its cursor is. Every weapon-employment procedure in this file's Weapons list follows the same pattern: make a sensor the SOI, move its SPI onto the target, optionally slave the other sensors to that SPI (China Hat FWD LONG), then employ the weapon.

systems_notes.topic: TGP (LITENING targeting pod) - HOTAS reference, Tank Killer
systems_notes.notes: With the TGP page as SOI: TMS FWD SHORT toggles Point/Area Track, TMS FWD LONG creates a SPI, TMS AFT SHORT autofocuses, TMS AFT LONG resets the SPI to the steerpoint, TMS RIGHT SHORT sets a markpoint, TMS RIGHT LONG makes the last markpoint the SPI. DMS FWD/AFT SHORT zooms in/out. Boat Switch cycles video mode (FWD = FLIR Black Hot, MIDDLE = CCD, AFT = FLIR White Hot). China Hat FWD SHORT toggles Wide/Narrow FOV, FWD LONG slaves all sensors to the SPI, AFT SHORT toggles Laser Spot Search.

The Maverick's own seeker head doubles as a sensor once it's selected on the DSMS and made SOI - its DLZ (Dynamic Launch Zone) staple on the HUD shows minimum/maximum range and time-of-flight. See this file's own Weapons list for the full IR/laser Maverick employment procedures; this note is just the sensor side.

HMD symbology is grouped into four categories: Basic (aircraft heading/altitude/airspeed/pitch, horizon line, crosshair, SPI line), Navigation (steerpoints and markpoints), Unit (nearby datalink contacts - the same ones the TAD shows), and Designation (whatever you've hooked or designated with the helmet/TGP). Each symbol's visibility (ON/OFF/OCLD) and cutoff range is configurable per profile - see the HMCS Power-Up & Profiles checklist.

With the HMCS as SOI (Coolie Hat DOWN): TMS FWD SHORT hooks the symbol under the crosshair, FWD LONG makes the hooked object/HDC the SPI, AFT SHORT un-hooks, AFT LONG resets the SPI to the steerpoint, RIGHT SHORT creates a markpoint at the HDC, RIGHT LONG makes the last markpoint the SPI. DMS FWD/AFT adjusts HMD brightness, LEFT SHORT shows the TGP feed on the HMD, RIGHT SHORT cycles profiles, RIGHT LONG slaves the TGP to the HMCS line-of-sight. China Hat FWD SHORT toggles TGP Wide/Narrow FOV, AFT SHORT recages the HDC to the crosshair.

The AN/ALQ-131 ECM pod has four jammer modes, cycled with the jammer mode selector button next to the RWR: AIR (counters most air-to-air radars), SAM1 (older-generation SAM systems like the SA-3/SA-6/SA-8), SAM2 (newer-generation SAM systems like the SA-10/SA-11/SA-15/SA-16, and the 2S6), AAA (radar-directed gun systems like the ZSU-23-4 and ZU-23). The jammer status readout shows SBY (standby, not jamming) or OPR plus the active mode (e.g. "OPR SAM1") when it's actually jamming - this is a separate system from the chaff/flare countermeasure programs (see the night-flying ground-prep checklist for those).

systems_notes.topic: RWR (Radar Warning Receiver) - reading the display
systems_notes.notes: The RWR shows a top-down view of radar emitters around you, friendly and enemy - the closer a symbol is to the center, the stronger that radar's signal. No circle around a symbol means that radar is searching, not tracking you. A steady circle means it's tracking/locked onto your aircraft - a missile could launch any second if it's a SAM site. A flashing circle means a missile is already in the air, guided by that radar - time to pop countermeasures and maneuver. PRI (Priority) mode limits the display to the 5 highest-priority contacts; SEP (Separate) spreads out overlapping symbols so they're easier to read individually.

The MWS reports one of three states: OFF (unpowered), ACTIVE (powered and watching), or LAUNCH (a missile has been detected heading at you - start evasive maneuvers and deploy countermeasures immediately). The RWR itself shows a launch the same way, as an "M" symbol with a circle around it, indicating the missile's direction of origin.

SADL puts the A-10 on the same digital picture as other friendly forces via the Army's EPLRS network - sharing position, identification, and target data automatically instead of only over voice radio. It needs the JTRS switch ON (see the post-start checklist) and your Group/Own ID set (see the SADL Network Setup checklist) before any of it works.

Flight Members (aircraft on your own Group ID) show as an icon with their Own ID and altitude, in thousands of feet. Friendly Networked Members (a different Group ID) show altitude only, no ID. Friendly Ground Forces need an EPLRS radio fitted to broadcast their position at all. A Mini-SPI is a smaller, single-tier version of the normal SPI symbol - someone else's SPI being broadcast to you, connected to their aircraft icon by a blue line.

Three radios on the left console: the ARC-210 (V/UHF, for air and ground units - replaces the Legacy VHF AM #1, which isn't installed on the Tank Killer variant), the ARC-186 VHF FM #2 (30.000-76.000 MHz, for JTAC units), and the ARC-164 UHF (225.000-399.975 MHz, for wingmen/support flights/ATC). The Mic Switch picks which one you transmit on: FWD = ARC-210, AFT = VHF FM, DOWN = UHF.

Routes audio, not transmission - each radio has its own volume, but the Intercom panel's Audio Control Switches (INT/FM/UHF/VHF/AIM/IFF/ILS/TCN) turn each one's receive audio on or off, plus LASTE warning tones. The Intercom Selector Switch picks which radio your microphone actually speaks to; INT alone lets you talk to ground crew (for arming/refueling calls).

Several physical controls on the ARC-210 panel do nothing in DCS: the TOD SND/RCV buttons, the GPS button, the LSKs, the RT Select button, TEST, ZERO, and both ECCM/ECCM MASTER positions. Don't spend time troubleshooting them - it's a limitation of the sim, not something you're doing wrong.

The A-10C's refueling door only works with a flying-boom tanker - in DCS, that's specifically the KC-135 Stratotanker. The other refueling aircraft in DCS (Il-78M, KC-135 MPRS, S-3B Viking, KC-130) are all probe-and-drogue systems, which the A-10C can't use.

Four main interfaces control navigation: the CDU/AAP, the CDU Page Repeater/UFC scratchpad, the NMSP, and HOTAS controls (which vary by whatever's currently SOI). The EGI (Embedded GPS & Inertial Navigation System) is the primary nav system, feeding the CDU with position/attitude/steering data. HARS (Heading & Attitude Reference System) is a gyro-based backup that takes over automatically if the EGI's INS fails - it can't drive the HUD's Total Velocity Vector and drifts under hard maneuvering, so there's no real reason to select it manually while the EGI is working.

The NMSP picks what feeds the HUD, ADI, and HSI. HARS and EGI are mutually exclusive - selecting one deselects the other. TISL, TACAN, and ILS are also mutually exclusive with each other (all three use external beacons/stations). STR PT mode makes the HSI/ADI operate relative to your steerpoint; ANCHR mode instead points them at the anchor point (bullseye). The UHF/FM Homing lights turn amber when their respective radio panel is set to homing mode.

The moving map has three scale modes: MAN (change scale manually with the ADJ +/- rocker), AUTO (scale follows the selected map chart format automatically), and OFF. With the TAD as SOI, China Hat FWD SHORT cycles NORM/EXP1/EXP2 map-expansion modes - each step narrows the displayed chart format by one increment (e.g. 1:2M to 1:1M to 1:500K) regardless of the TAD's own range-scale setting. Key TAD symbols: a green diamond marks where the TGP is pointed, range rings are centered on your own aircraft (the outer ring matches the TAD's range-scale setting), and the bullseye/anchor point has its own dedicated symbol.

With the TAD as SOI (Coolie Hat toward its MFCD): TMS FWD SHORT hooks a symbol (SPI, TGP diamond, waypoint/steerpoint, or bullseye), AFT SHORT un-hooks it, LEFT LONG broadcasts your SPI. DMS FWD/AFT SHORT changes TAD scale, FWD LONG toggles the quick map view, AFT LONG selects the TAD center option, LEFT SHORT toggles CEN/DEP mode, RIGHT SHORT cycles center/depressed mode. China Hat FWD SHORT toggles the expanded map mode, AFT SHORT resets the TAD cursor. The Slew Control Switch moves the TAD cursor.

The HSI is the fallback for navigation data not shown on the HUD or CDU, and for use after battle damage. Bearing Pointer 1 shows the magnetic bearing to the selected TACAN station (or the ADF station instead, if ADF is selected - ADF takes priority if both are active); Bearing Pointer 2 points to the current steerpoint. The CDI (Course Deviation Indicator) shows how far off your selected course you are, with a TO-FROM flag telling you which side of the station/waypoint you're on. The Course Set Knob dials in a course; the Heading Set Knob sets the heading bug.

Waypoints are pre-planned reference points (up to 2,050 in the CDU database) that you can create, edit, and string into flight plans. A Steerpoint is just whichever waypoint or markpoint is currently selected. Markpoints mark a point of interest on the fly (up to 26, lettered A-Z). An Anchor Point (Bullseye) is a shared reference point for the whole friendly force. The AAP Steerpoint Selector Knob picks which pool of points you're browsing (MISSION = all waypoints, FLT PLAN = the active flight plan's waypoints, MARK = markpoints, ANCHR = the anchor point), and the AAP CDU Selector Knob picks what the CDU page shows (OTHER unlocks the Function Select Keys for adding/editing anything, POSITION shows your own position, STEER shows the current steerpoint, WAYPT shows a specific waypoint/markpoint).

A bullseye call communicates your position without telling the enemy where you actually are, since only friendly forces know where the bullseye is: bearing from the bullseye, then range from the bullseye, then altitude - e.g. "Bullseye 180 for 15, angels 20."

The DSMS replaces the old A-10A armament control panel: every weapon setting, release parameter and armament control now lives on DSMS pages on an MFCD. It shows overall weapons status, the inventory on each station, which stations are selected, the arm state, the gun's status and which profile is active for each weapon. Open it with the lower OSB labeled DSMS. Its sub-pages are Status, Profile (main, control and settings), Inventory (main, select, class, store type and store select), Selective Jettison and Missile Control (mode, power and boresight for the Maverick and AIM-9). A profile is one weapon plus its delivery settings; pick profiles on the DSMS page or with DMS LEFT/RIGHT while the HUD is SOI.

Every station and the gun are color-coded so you can read weapon status at a glance. White = Master Arm SAFE (systems behave as if armed, but no weapons or flares are released; a Maverick shows no video). Blue = Master Arm TRAIN (simulated 'virtual' weapons - TRAIN profiles never show mismatch errors). Green = Master Arm ARM. A selected weapon takes the arm-state color. Red = the profile and the inventory disagree about what's on that station, or the profile has invalid settings - after re-arming, run the 'dsms reload after rearm' checklist to clear a mismatch.

systems_notes.topic: Rearm / re-arming - reload the DSMS from the DTC
systems_notes.notes: After the ground crew rearms the jet, the DSMS does not know what's on the pylons until you reload it: the crew installs a fresh Data Transfer Cartridge (DTC) with the new ordnance, and the DSMS has to load it before its station data updates. Until you do, stations can show red (profile/inventory mismatch). The step-by-step is the 'dsms reload after rearm' checklist in the Checklists tab (MSG page - LOAD - DTS UPLOAD - LOAD ALL).

Five HUD master modes, cycled with the Master Mode Control Button on the stick. NAV: navigation data only, no weapon symbology. GUNS: selectable gunsight options. CCIP: bombing symbology for Continuously Computed Impact Point delivery, including the consent-to-release modes (Maverick delivery also uses CCIP). CCRP: Continuously Computed Release Point symbology for illumination flares, unguided bombs, laser-guided bombs and Inertially Aided Munitions. AIR-TO-AIR: gun and AIM-9 symbology - the only mode you can't reach by tapping; hold the button for about 3 seconds.

There are two ways to deliver bombs. CCIP is traditional dive bombing: you dive at the target and the reticle shows where the bomb will impact - precise, but the lower you go, the more exposed you are to anything defending the target. CCRP lets you fly straight and level: the HUD tells you when to release on the target you designated (usually with the TGP) - safer, but somewhat less precise. Which to use is up to the situation and your preference; the delivery mode is set per weapon in the DSMS profile, ideally during preflight.

Set with the CCIP CONSENT option in the IFFCC TEST menu. OFF = manual release (MAN REL): the weapon leaves the moment you press the Weapon Release Button. 3/9 = the Solution Cue must pass through the reticle before the weapon releases. 5 MIL = the Solution Cue must pass over the reticle pipper. Entering the IFFCC TEST menu resets the HUD master mode to GUNS, so set the IFFCC back to ON and pick your master mode afterward.

systems_notes.topic: How to fire a weapon - the basic sequence
systems_notes.notes: The same six steps apply to every weapon. 1) Select the weapon on the DSMS page. 2) Select its profile: make the HUD SOI (Coolie Hat UP), then press DMS LEFT/RIGHT to cycle profiles. 3) Arm the weapon and its sensors. 4) Choose the delivery mode if the weapon has one (CCIP or CCRP). 5) Use a sensor (make it SOI) to find the target, put the SPI on it, slave the other sensors to the SPI and lock. 6) Fire once you have a firing solution.
